title: Smoothness of the principal localization of the prepared Popescu quotient
statement: Let R and Cbar be commutative rings, with an R-algebra structure and an R/pi^2R-algebra structure on Cbar, and pi an element of R. Let d be prepared polynomial data [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lift-preparation], and define its explicit quotient D=ULift(R[x,z]/(f_j-pi z_j, a_k z_l-sum_{j in E_k}h_{klj}z_j-pi g_{kl})). Then the principal localization D[1/pi] is a smooth R-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. No Noetherian or annihilator hypothesis and no special-fibre maps are required.

source.place: Stacks Project, Tag 07CP (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07CP), key equality and property (b).

proof.text: Let P=R[x], A=P[1/pi], and t be the canonical inverse of pi in A. Define F:R[x,z] to A by x_i mapping to its polynomial class and z_j mapping to t f_j. The restriction of F to P is the localization map. The primary equations f_j-pi z_j vanish because pi t=1.

Apply the polynomial localization map to the Prepared relation a_k f_l=sum_{j in E_k}h_{klj}f_j+pi^2 g_{kl}. Since t pi^2=pi, the substituted auxiliary equation is t times the difference between the two sides of this relation, hence zero. Every generator of the defining ideal is killed, so F descends through the explicit quotient and ULift and extends to f:D[1/pi] to A.

The original-variable inclusion into D[1/pi] extends to g:A to D[1/pi] because pi is a unit. The composite f g fixes P and hence fixes A by localization extensionality. For g f, the primary quotient relations imply f_j=pi z_j, while the image of t is the inverse of pi, so the composite fixes both x_i and z_j. Polynomial, quotient, ULift and localization extensionality show g f is the identity. These explicit inverse maps give an R-algebra equivalence A to D[1/pi].

P is formally smooth and finitely presented over R by the Mathlib polynomial instances. A is smooth over P by principal localization, so it is smooth over R by composition. Transport smoothness along the explicit equivalence to D[1/pi].

theorem popescu_lift_smooth_away (R : Type a) (Cbar : Type c)

    Smooth R (Localization.Away (algebraMap R d.liftingAlgebra π))
